verdicts.note: Attacked toward -2 and toward 0. Toward -2: she holds the seat and lists four other local boards (S1). Toward 0: she has held the seat by appointment only since February 2026 (S2), and she lost the 2020 race for it (S5). A short-tenure sitting commissioner who runs on 'practical experience' and 'steady, informed leadership' (S1) fits -1, and medium confidence fits that ambiguity. S1 and S2 are in her frontmatter and support the basis. Display: office_does matches _contest.md (S2; two years left in the term). The race blurb matches the dossiers (appointed after Nelson resigned, S6 and S7 in _contest.md; Blachly on the planning commission; primary 186 to 119, S4). Minor defects: (1) the first highlight cites S2 for 'after Jim Nelson resigned', but Mulrony's dossier attributes only the appointment and 'first woman' to S2; the resignation is sourced to S6 in _contest.md. (2) The summary calls her a 'former' dental hygiene professor and insurance agent, but the dossier lists her career without dates and does not say whether she still works at the Obenland & Low agency.

Attacked as overreading a generic line. 'Strong financial oversight, and steady, informed leadership are essential' (S1) maps directly to pole_a's 'oversight' wording. The primary dossier's appointment record also has her naming financial responsibility and balancing the budget (S8, not re-read), which points the same way. Nothing in the dossier points to expansion. One statement, worded in the rubric's own language, supports -1 at medium. S1 is in her frontmatter. Highlights match S1 and S6.

The direction holds: he is the challenger and has never held county office (S1). The confidence is overstated, though. His statement does not make an outsider or new-voices pitch. It sells experience: a 29-year agribusiness career, being 'results focused, with experience in management of large budgets', and ten years on the conservation district board plus a planning commission seat (S1). The incumbent he faces was appointed only in February 2026. The +1 rests on his challenger status alone, so low confidence fits better. S1 is in his frontmatter. Display: the summary and all four highlights match the dossier: 15 years at WinField United after 14 at Pomeroy Grain Growers, conservation district vice chair, planning commission, the balanced-budget quote and the property-rights quote (all S1).

Attacked toward -1: 'long term balanced budget funding' and 'management of large budgets' (S1) lean toward restraint. Toward +1: the same sentence's purpose is the 'continuation of the high standards' of road and emergency services (S1). That is maintenance, not expansion, and he names no new program. Restraint language serving service continuity nets to 0. Medium confidence is acceptable because the dossier records both halves in a single statement. S1 is in his frontmatter. No missing scores proposed: his property-rights line has no rubric axis (housing is about affordability, not property rights), and neither dossier has taxes or reform evidence.
